kernel store lock is released, including worker cleanup. Concurrent/repeated
stops coalesce. Cleanup failure rejects. `serve DIR --wait-stopped` exposes the
five-second read-only lock barrier; it never signals a PID or initializes a
store. Deploy/rollback also wait before admission for a shutting-down owner;
live serve still uses authenticated control. Ambiguous activation is not retried.

`data TABLE --json` now returns `{rows, more, limit}` including empty results.
The default limit is 50. Check `more` before interpreting a row count; increase
`--limit N` for a larger inspection. Text output stays JSON lines. This replaces
the previous bare JSON array so stdout-only callers can detect truncation.
# Client: answers stay on screen

**Start here:** `useQueryData`/`useQueryResult` ([short screens](CLIENT-AND-OPERATIONS.md#short-screens)); metadata: `useQuery`/`usePage`; `useFollowing` (`guide feeds`); lists: `ReadState`.

```tsx
import { matchRead, readPresentation, usePage } from "snapback4/react";
import { api } from "../snapback/generated/api";
export function Inbox() { const page = usePage(api.inboxCards, {}), status = readPresentation(page.read); return <>{matchRead(page.read, { loading: () => "Loading…", denied: why => why.message,
    absent: () => "No conversations", partial: () => "Partial results", present: rows => `${rows.length} conversations` })}
    {status.incomplete && "Results may be incomplete"}{page.items.map(row => <p key={row.id}>{row.title} ({row.memberCount})</p>)}<button disabled={!page.hasMore} onClick={page.loadMore}>More</button></>;
}
```

- `E_OFFLINE`: unavailable; reconnect.
- `E_QUERY_RETRY`: exhausted; retry.

## Reference

`Write`: pending custody, fresh sent result, replay without result, or failed. Clear on sentResult; undefined is not success.
```tsx
import { useState } from "react"; import { matchRead, sentResult, useAppReady, useMutation, useQuery } from "snapback4/react";
import { api } from "../snapback/generated/api";
export function Composer({conversationId}:{conversationId:string}) {
  const [draft,setDraft]=useState(""),[submitted,setSubmitted]=useState("");
  const ready=useAppReady(),send=useMutation(api.send),member=useQuery(api.myMembership,{conversationId});
  const blocked=matchRead(member,{denied:()=>true,absent:read=>read.fresh&&!read.revalidating,partial:()=>false,otherwise:()=>false});
  async function submit(){const text=draft.trim();if(!ready||blocked||!text||text.length>2000)return;setSubmitted(text);const write=await send.run({conversationId,body:text});if(sentResult(write)!==undefined)setDraft(current=>current.trim()===text?"":current);}
  return <><input value={draft} onChange={e=>setDraft(e.target.value)}/>
    <button disabled={!ready||send.inFlight||blocked} onClick={()=>void submit()}>Send</button>
    {send.last?.state==="failed"&&submitted&&<p role="alert">Not sent: {submitted} <button onClick={()=>setDraft(current=>current?current+" "+submitted:submitted)}>Edit</button> <button onClick={()=>setSubmitted("")}>Dismiss</button></p>}</>;
}
```
Membership: no horizon, the conversation's own group and messages' audience prove existence unless a pending prediction blocks absence. `loading` means acquisition or later withdrawal. `existence(member) === "absent"` blocks only when fresh and non-revalidating; denied blocks; loading/partial never disable. Never add `with own keys` to admin-written memberships.
Draft/receipt owners: [reference](CLIENT-AND-OPERATIONS.md). `waitSeconds:0` returns custody; keep the original id, never auto-resend.

## An online role form across releases
Own createApp({url,writes:"online",sessionStore:localStorageSessionStore()}) outside render under AppProvider.
```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react"; import { isPresent, matchReadList, sentResult, useAppReady, useMutation, useQuery, useRelease } from "snapback4/react"; import { api } from "../snapback/generated/api";
export function StaffWorkspace({team}: {team: string}) {
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState(""), [selected, setSelected] = useState("");
  const ready = useAppReady(), release = useRelease(), role = useQuery(api.myRole, {team});
  const [lastStaff, setLastStaff] = useState(false);
  const staff = api.myRole.available(release) && isPresent(role) && role.complete && role.fresh && !role.revalidating && role.data.role === "staff", uncertain = "loading" in role || ("data" in role && (role.existence === "partial" || !role.complete || !role.fresh || role.revalidating === true));
  useEffect(() => { if (!uncertain) setLastStaff(staff); }, [uncertain, staff]);
  const shell = uncertain ? lastStaff : staff;
  const available = api.addStaffNote.available(release) && api.staffNotes.available(release), add = useMutation(api.addStaffNote);
  async function submit() {const title = draft.trim(); if (!ready || !staff || !available || !title || !selected) return;
    const write = await add.run({team, title, category:selected}); if (sentResult(write) !== undefined) setDraft(current => current === draft ? "" : current);}
  return <section aria-label="Staff workspace"><p>{shell ? "Staff workspace" : "Staff access required"}</p>
    <label>Note<input value={draft} onChange={e => setDraft(e.target.value)} /></label>
    <label htmlFor="category">Category</label><select id="category" value={selected} onChange={e => setSelected(e.target.value)}><option value="">Choose</option><option value="general">General</option></select>
    <button disabled={!ready || !staff || !available || add.inFlight} onClick={() => void submit()}>Save note</button>
    {staff && available ? <StaffRows team={team} /> : <p>{"denied" in role || "denied" in release || ("generation" in release && !available) || (!uncertain && !staff) ? "Staff workspace not available" : "Waiting for staff capabilities"}</p>}
    {add.last?.state === "failed" && <p role="alert">{add.last.why.message}</p>}
  </section>;
}
function StaffRows({team}: {team:string}) {
  const rows = useQuery(api.staffNotes, {team}); return <>{matchReadList(rows, {denied: why => <p role="alert">{why.message}</p>, absent: () => <p>No notes</p>,
    present: notes => <ul>{notes.map(row => <li key={row.id}>{row.title} — {row.priority ?? "normal"}</li>)}</ul>,
    otherwise: () => <p>Updating notes…</p>})}</>;
}
```
Mount `<StaffWorkspace key={team} team={team}/>`: drafts survive loading/releases; resources/accounts/backends reset them. Sticky role labels the shell; fresh/complete/non-revalidating role and availability gate reads/Save. Rules decide permission. Optional since-release fields need fallbacks: `row.priority ?? "normal"`.

## A public guest page

Guests (`use identity`/`use identity guests`): public reads require browser session custody.
```tsx
import { createApp } from "snapback4/app";
import { localStorageSessionStore } from "snapback4/auth";
import { AppProvider, matchReadList, useAuth, useQuery } from "snapback4/react";
import { api } from "../snapback/generated/api";
const guestApp = createApp({url:"http://127.0.0.1:4400", readOnly:true, sessionStore:localStorageSessionStore()});
export function GuestPage() { return <AppProvider app={guestApp}><GuestGate /></AppProvider>; }
function GuestGate() {
  const auth = useAuth();
  if (auth.state === "restoring") return <p>Restoring…</p>;
  if (auth.state === "signed-out") return <><button onClick={() => void auth.guest()}>Continue as a guest</button><p role="alert">{auth.why?.message}</p></>;
  return <PublicNotes />;
}
function PublicNotes() {
  const notes = useQuery(api.publicNotes, {});
  return <>{matchReadList(notes, {denied: why => <p role="alert">{why.message}</p>, absent: () => <p>No public notes</p>,
    present: rows => <ul>{rows.map(row => <li key={row.id}>{row.title}</li>)}</ul>, otherwise: () => <p>Loading…</p>})}</>;
}
```

## React hooks and auth decisions

Render sign-in controls while signed-out, Restoring… otherwise. AppProvider resets on app/viewer changes. `useAppReady()` marks successful initial opening after app.ready; release switches/admission warnings preserve it. Restoration, sign-out and app/account replacement reset it; initial failure recovers on sign-in. Keep drafts above role/release gates. Readiness grants no permission/admission.
`writes:"online"` with device/readOnly yields signed-out `useAuth().why` and failed app.ready. Recreate corrected. Missing browser storage still throws `E_ADMISSION`.
`useAuth()` members: `state`, `viewer`, `why`, `signup(email, password)`, `login(email, password)`, `guest()`, `logout()`, `logoutEverywhere()`. `signOut()` belongs to the client. Expo session store: secureStoreSessionStore(SecureStore); password form: [reference](CLIENT-AND-OPERATIONS.md#password-react-and-expo).

| Helper | Input/result | Handlers/arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `matchRead(read, handlers)` | Read or page; handler result | `loading(read)`, `denied(why,read)`, `absent(read)`, `partial(data,read)`, `present(data,read)`. Bare `why: Refusal`; data first, metadata second. All five required, even partial on single rows; `otherwise(read)` replaces omitted loading/absent/present only. |
| `matchReadList(read, handlers)` | List read or page | Requires `denied(why,read)` and `otherwise(read)`; omitted partial uses otherwise. |
| `otherwiseAll(fallback, overrides?)` | Spread into matchRead handlers | `fallback(read)` includes denied/partial; named handlers win in any order. |
| `usePage(op, args)` | Query with `c: cursor ?`; omit c from args | `{read, items, hasMore, loadMore}`; match page.read/page, render items, call loadMore(). No handlers. |

`'data' in read` exposes data/existence/metadata. Complete empty lists are absent. `isPresent` excludes null; `isReady` permits it; `existence(read)` and `read.existence` classify. `absent` can be an authorised empty list. PDFs require a `doc: file <=10000000 ?` column; persist uploaded ids through mutations (`guide assets`).
```ts
import type { Read, Client } from "snapback4/contract";
export function listLabel(read: Read<readonly {id:string}[]>): string {
  if ('denied' in read) return "not available"; if ('data' in read) return read.existence === "absent" ? "No rows" : `${read.data.length} rows`; return "Loading…"; }
export async function uploadPdf(client: Client, picked: File) { return client.upload(picked, {file: {type: "application/pdf", name: picked.name}}); }
```
`loading`: keep shells; `denied`: show refusal; `present`: render; `absent`: proven empty; `partial`: uncertain. Offline absent is absence at the acquired watermark. Hidden/missing rows are indistinguishable. `readPresentation` notices never grant permission. Unknown counts never hide conversations.
`predicts`: eligible/device/held facts may render `pending:true` before `useMutation().run()` settles; others queue without rows. Never/online data follows settlement/delivery. run() waits for sent/failed; `{waitSeconds:0}` returns custody. Proofs await fresh sent; predictions aren't settlement.
`query(op,args)` settles ready/denied within 30 seconds. Unavailable offline reads give immediate `E_OFFLINE`. After four rounds, exhaustion refuses retryable `E_QUERY_RETRY`; permanently unavailable held reads refuse non-retryable `E_QUERY_HELD`. Retention, RowOf/ArgsOf/ResultOf and {skip}: [reference](CLIENT-AND-OPERATIONS.md). Share/paginate: eight active, eight queued observation attempts; direct queries and timed presence refreshes use separate paths.
Browser createApp: no sync → journal; sync → webDevice(); online writes: writes:"online". Native: nativeDevice; Expo Go online. Expo setup/pins/upgrade: guide expo. Regenerate iOS/rebuild after native changes; every milestone: npm run export:ios; proof in the background: witness status --wait. Rebuild: npm run native:smoke. Acquisition/offline reopen/reconnect/write replay: guide witness.
useOnline: server reads/ephemeral/actions; durable writes: app.mutate. SDK owns delivery reporting; screen owns visible `seen` reporting; useSeen retries receipts (guide receipts). Read-only: guide read-only. Media: OFFLINE-UPLOADS.md. Proofs: await fresh sent, then rendering; avoid networkidle (guide testing).
Keyed counts: hidden key → null; authorized missing count group → 0; public → number. Choose count ?? 0 explicitly.
## Proof API (generated from source)

Every runtime and type export of `snapback4/proof` is listed below. Signatures, result fields and failure reasons are generated from TypeScript declarations and their @throws comments; qualification checks this table against the source. Playwright types such as Page and Locator come from playwright-core.

  for (const name of ["docker", "podman"]) {

    // An isolated flake rerun cannot turn the original suite into a release pass.

    // cannot produce the receipt publication imports as suite qualification.

      if (cleanSource(root) !== source || sri(client) !== clientIntegrity || sri(expo) !== expoIntegrity)
        throw new Error("release source or client changed during consumer qualification");
      copyFileSync(tarball, join(out, packed.filename));

        suite: { status: "not-run" }, publicationQualified: false };
      save(join(out, "consumer.json"), evidence);
      console.log(JSON.stringify(evidence, null, 2));
      return evidence;
    }
    if (!suitePassed) throw new Error(`Linux source suite failed: ${summary ?? result.error?.message ?? result.status}; see ${log}; consumer evidence in proofs.json (no qualification receipt)`);
    const cc = process.env.SNAPBACK4_MUSL_CC ?? join(process.env.HOME, ".local/share/snapback4-musl-1.2.5/bin/musl-gcc");
    const receipt = { format: 1, route: runtime, source, target: linuxTarget, toolchain: { rustc: run("rustc", ["-Vv"]).trim(), cargo: run("cargo", ["-V"]).trim(), cc: run(cc, ["--version"]).trim(), linker: cc }, flags: { LIBSQLITE3_FLAGS: sqliteBuildFlags, RUSTFLAGS: linuxRustFlags }, suite: { status: "passed", exitCode: result.status, summary }, proofs, regressions, day2Proof, day4Proof, day5Proof, productionProofs, proofKit, clientRecipes, ruleRecipes, frontendProofs, starterProofs, stagingProof, migrationProof, securityProof, elf, platform, binarySha256, clientIntegrity, expo: artifact(expo, "snapback4-expo", version) };

    validateLinux(receipt, tarball, { version, integrity: clientIntegrity }, source);
    copyFileSync(tarball, join(out, packed.filename));
    save(join(out, "receipt.json"), receipt);
    console.log(JSON.stringify(receipt, null, 2));
    return receipt;
  } finally { rmSync(work, { recursive: true, force: true }); }

#!/usr/bin/env node
// `npx snapback4 <verb>`: the Rust binary, found in the platform package
// installed beside this one, or named by SNAPBACK4_BIN, or built in this
// repository. The JavaScript here only finds and runs it, and the two live and
// die together: SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP to this wrapper are forwarded, and
// SIGKILL, which cannot be forwarded, still stops the binary: it is told this
// wrapper's PID (SNAPBACK4_SUPERVISOR_PID) and exits when its parent is gone
// (Linux: the kernel's parent-death signal; elsewhere within 250 ms). So a
// recorded PID of either stops the server; `GET /dev/status` reports both
// (`pid` is the binary, `wrapperPid` this wrapper), and so does the stderr line
// `SNAPBACK4_READY … url=… pid=… wrapperPid=…`.
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { resolveBinary } from "../dist/resolve-binary.js";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { constants } from "node:os";
import { firstCheckWarnings } from "./upgrade-warnings.js";

if (process.argv[2] === "check" && !process.argv.includes("--help")) firstCheckWarnings();

if (process.argv[2] === "web-shell") {
  try { await (await import("./web-shell.js")).runWebShell(process.argv.slice(3)); }
  catch (error) { console.error(`E_INPUT at web-shell: ${error.message}\n  rewrite: export a static app, then run snapback4 web-shell dist --base /`); process.exit(2); }
  process.exit(0);
}

let binary;
try { binary = resolveBinary(); }
catch (error) { console.error(error.message); process.exit(2); }
// Internal export helpers share the wrapper's kernel lease through fd 3.
const exportLease = process.argv[2] === "witness" && ["export-lease", "export-publish"].includes(process.argv[3]);
const child = spawn(binary, process.argv.slice(2), { stdio: exportLease ? ["inherit", "inherit", "inherit", 3] : "inherit", env: {
  ...process.env, SNAPBACK4_ACQUIRE_HELPER: fileURLToPath(new URL("./witness-acquire.js", import.meta.url)),
  SNAPBACK4_UPGRADE_HELPER: fileURLToPath(new URL("./upgrade.js", import.meta.url)),
  SNAPBACK4_WEB_HELPER: fileURLToPath(new URL("./witness-web.js", import.meta.url)),
  SNAPBACK4_SUPERVISOR_PID: String(process.pid),
} });
const handlers = new Map(["SIGINT", "SIGTERM", "SIGHUP"].map(signal => [signal, () => { try { child.kill(signal); } catch { /* gone */ } }]));
for (const [signal, handler] of handlers) process.on(signal, handler);
// `npx snapback4 dev` puts npm and `sh -c` above this wrapper. A SIGTERM to the
// npx PID kills npm and the shell but never reaches us, so the server would keep
// serving as an orphan. Our parent's death is the stop signal. (`process.ppid` is
// read once at startup, so probe the original parent instead.)
const parent = process.ppid;
const parentAlive = () => { try { process.kill(parent, 0); return true; } catch (error) { return error.code === "EPERM"; } };
const orphanWatch = parent > 1 ? setInterval(() => {
  if (!parentAlive()) { try { child.kill("SIGTERM"); } catch { /* gone */ } }
}, 250) : null;
orphanWatch?.unref();
child.on("exit", (code, signal) => {
  if (orphanWatch) clearInterval(orphanWatch);
  for (const [name, handler] of handlers) process.off(name, handler);
  if (signal) {
    // Restore the default disposition before re-raising. Some platforms do not
    // terminate on this call; never let their empty event loop report success.
    const status = 128 + (constants.signals[signal] ?? { SIGHUP: 1, SIGINT: 2, SIGTERM: 15 }[signal] ?? 1);
    setTimeout(() => process.exit(status), 100);
    try { process.kill(process.pid, signal); } catch { process.exit(status); }
    return;
  }
  process.exit(code ?? 1);
});

+## List read state
+
+`ReadState` from snapback4/react renders a list read or `usePage` result in one
+expression. Loading/empty default to null; omitted denied throws QueryRefusal.
+Empty describes returned rows, including partial/stale lists, not proven absence.
+The data renderer receives the same precise read metadata. Supply Text/View
+slots in React Native; the component creates no observation or retained state.
+
+```tsx
+import { ReadState, type Read } from "snapback4/react";
+export function ListScreen({ read }: { read: Read<readonly { id: string; title: string }[]> }) {
+  return <ReadState read={read} loading={<p>Loading…</p>} empty={<p>No results</p>} denied={why => <p role="alert">{why.message}</p>}>{(rows, answer) => <ul data-complete={answer.complete}>{rows.map(row => <li key={row.id}>{row.title}</li>)}</ul>}</ReadState>;
+}
+```

//! Query result paths and nullable reads of private side tables.
use super::*;

pub(super) const VIEWER_KEY: &str = "$lookupViewerKey";
const TARGET_ROW: &str = "$lookupTargetRow";

// @ref LLP 3000.036.002#151-evidence-and-decision — compatibility keeps
// fallthrough null; check must name a concrete uncovered source path.
pub(super) fn fallthrough(decl: &ast::ProgramDecl) -> Diagnostic {
    fn path(body: &[S], implicit: bool) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
        let mut route = Vec::new();
        for (at, stmt) in body.iter().enumerate() {
            match stmt {
                S::Return { .. } => return None,
                S::Expr { .. } if implicit && at + 1 == body.len() => return None,
                S::Require { condition: A::Literal { value: Literal::Bool(false), .. }, .. } => return None,
                S::If { then_body, else_body, site, .. } => {
                    let completes = implicit && at + 1 == body.len();
                    let (arm, rest) = if let Some(rest) = path(then_body, completes) { ("true", rest) }
                        else if let Some(rest) = path(else_body, completes) { ("false", rest) }
                        else { return None };
                    route.push(format!("if at {site} is {arm}")); route.extend(rest);
                }
                S::For { site, .. } => route.push(format!("loop at {site} has zero iterations")),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Some(route)
    }
    let route = path(&decl.body, true).unwrap_or_default();
    let route = if route.is_empty() { "entry → end".into() } else { format!("{} → end", route.join(" → ")) };
    Diagnostic::new(&decl.site, "N_QUERY_FALLTHROUGH",
        format!("query {} can finish without a result ({route}); that path returns null", decl.name),
        "return a value on this path: add `return []` for an intentionally empty list, or `return null` for intentional absence; a return inside a possibly empty loop does not cover its zero-iteration path").guide("programs")
}

impl Binder<'_> {
    fn lookup_rule_proved(&self, value: &A) -> bool {
        let mut copy = value.clone();
        let mut target = false;
        super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut copy, &mut |node| {
            if matches!(node, A::Name { name, .. } if name == TARGET_ROW) { target = true; }
        });
        if !target { return self.point_guard_safe(value) && self.authorization_proved(value, true); }
        match value {
            A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "or" => self.lookup_rule_proved(left) || self.lookup_rule_proved(right),
            A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "and" => self.lookup_rule_proved(left) && self.lookup_rule_proved(right),
            _ => false,
        }
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#152-lookup-contract-and-diagnostics — transport
    // only source advice facts across the helper's captured argument boundary.
    pub(super) fn helper_lookup_points(&self, function: &ast::FunctionDecl, args: &[A]) -> Vec<ReadExpr> {
        fn closed(value: &A, parameters: &[ast::ArgDecl]) -> bool {
            let mut value = value.clone();
            let mut safe = true;
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut value, &mut |node| match node {
                A::Name { name, .. } if name != "viewer" && name != "now" && !parameters.iter().any(|p| p.name == *name) => safe = false,
                A::Focal { .. } | A::Write { .. } | A::Call { .. } => safe = false,
                _ => {}
            });
            safe
        }
        fn substitute(value: &mut A, parameters: &[ast::ArgDecl], args: &[A]) {
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(value, &mut |node| {
                if let A::Name { name, .. } = node && let Some(at) = parameters.iter().position(|p| p.name == *name)
                    && let Some(argument) = args.get(at) { *node = argument.clone(); }
            });
        }
        fn collect(catalog: &Catalog, function: &ast::FunctionDecl, args: &[A], stack: &mut Vec<String>, fuel: &mut usize, reads: &mut Vec<ReadExpr>) {
            if stack.len() >= 32 || stack.contains(&function.name) { return; }
            stack.push(function.name.clone());
            let mut body = match &function.body { ast::FunctionBody::Block(body) => body.clone(), ast::FunctionBody::Expression(value) => vec![S::Return { value: value.clone(), site: value.site().clone() }] };
            super::super::intent_walk::statements(&mut body, &mut |node| {
                if *fuel == 0 { return; } *fuel -= 1;
                match node {
                    A::Read(read) if read.keys.iter().all(|key| closed(&key.value, &function.args)) => {
                        let mut value = A::Read(read.clone()); substitute(&mut value, &function.args, args);
                        if let A::Read(read) = value { reads.push(read); }
                    }
                    A::Call { name, args: arguments, .. } if arguments.iter().all(|value| closed(value, &function.args)) => {
                        if let Some(callee) = catalog.functions.get(name) {
                            let mut arguments = arguments.clone();
                            for value in &mut arguments { substitute(value, &function.args, args); }
                            collect(catalog, callee, &arguments, stack, fuel, reads);
                        }
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
            });
            stack.pop();
        }
        if self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Mutation { return Vec::new(); }
        let identity: Vec<_> = function.args.iter().map(|p| A::Name { name: p.name.clone(), site: p.site.clone() }).collect();
        let mut reads = Vec::new();
        collect(self.catalog, function, &identity, &mut Vec::new(), &mut 512, &mut reads);
        reads.into_iter().filter(|read| read.keys.iter().all(|key| closed(&key.value, &function.args))).filter(|read| {
            let mut value = A::Read(read.clone()); substitute(&mut value, &function.args, args);
            let A::Read(actual) = value else { return false };
            self.point_guard_safe(&A::Read(actual.clone())) && (self.point_present(&actual) || self.lookup_point_present(&actual) || self.row_independent_read_proved(&actual.table))
        }).collect()
    }
    // This marker suppresses advice only; it cannot authorize a runtime read
    // or enter the binder's authority/presence proof domains.
    pub(super) fn lookup_viewer_key(&self, value: &A) -> bool {
        if matches!(value, A::Name { name, .. } if name == "viewer" || self.binding(name)
            .is_some_and(|binding| binding.fields.contains_key(&vec![VIEWER_KEY.into()]))) { return true; }
        let equal = A::Binary { op: "=".into(), left: Box::new(value.clone()), right: Box::new(A::Name { name: "viewer".into(), site: value.site().clone() }), site: value.site().clone() };
        self.point_guard_safe(value) && self.authorization_proved(&equal, true)
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#10-wave-20-loop-repairs-dx5 — asserted and same-table reads still need reader authority; blind writes do not pass here.
    pub(super) fn optional_lookup_note(&mut self, read: &ReadExpr, point: &Read) {
        if self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Mutation || self.point_present(read) || self.lookup_point_present(read)
            || self.row_independent_read_proved(&read.table) { return; }
        let table = &self.schema.tables[&read.table];
        if table.ephemeral.is_some() || self.schema.maintain_for(&read.table).is_some() { return; }
        let index = &table.indexes[&point.index];
        let pinned = index.components.iter().zip(&point.key).filter_map(|(part, value)| part.column().map(|name| (name, value))).collect();
        if snapback4_core::engine::rules::prefix_visibility(&read.table, table, &table.rules.read, &pinned).decided_true { return; }
        if let Some(rule) = self.catalog.tables[&read.table].decl.rules.iter().find(|rule| rule.effect == ast::Effect::Read) {
            let named = read.keys.iter().all(|key| key.column.is_some());
            let keys: BTreeMap<_, _> = read.keys.iter().enumerate().filter_map(|(at, key)|
                Some((if named { key.column.clone()? } else { index.components.get(at)?.column()?.clone() },
                    if self.lookup_viewer_key(&key.value) { A::Name { name: "viewer".into(), site: key.site.clone() } } else { key.value.clone() }))).collect();
            let mut condition = rule.value.clone();
            // Rule constants and target fields occupy their own namespaces.
            // Freeze/seal them before injecting lexical caller key expressions.
            maintain_types::normalize_rule_constants(&mut condition);
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut condition, &mut |value| {
                if let A::Member { base, .. } = value && let A::Focal { site } = base.as_ref() {
                    **base = A::Name { name: TARGET_ROW.into(), site: site.clone() };
                }
            });
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut condition, &mut |value| {
                if let A::Member { base, name, .. } = value && matches!(base.as_ref(), A::Name { name, .. } if name == TARGET_ROW)
                    && let Some(key) = keys.get(name) { *value = key.clone(); }
            });
            if self.lookup_rule_proved(&condition) { return; }
        }
        let rule = table.through.as_ref().map_or_else(|| format!("read <- {}", table.rules.read.quarry()), |through| format!("read through .{}", through.reference));
        let location = self.catalog.tables[&read.table].decl.rules.iter().find(|rule| rule.effect == ast::Effect::Read)
            .map(|rule| rule.site.to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|| self.catalog.tables[&read.table].decl.site.to_string());
        if self.notes.iter().any(|note| note.code == "N_LOOKUP_FILTERED" && note.site == read.site) { return; }
        self.notes.push(Diagnostic::new(&read.site, "N_LOOKUP_FILTERED",
            format!("mutation {}: lookup of {} uses `{rule}` ({location}); its key and preceding guards do not prove read authority. A hidden, expired or missing row returns null; `! else CODE` refuses with that authored code for all three. A later field/default or require may report a different business condition", self.name, read.table),
            "review whether these callers should read this data; use a deliberately readable projection containing only the needed fields, or keep null as intentional absence. An id and a later write rule do not grant read authority; do not widen private rows just to read one field").guide("rules"));
    }
}

import { requireOptionalNativeModule } from "expo-modules-core";
import { createWitness, type Witness, type WitnessContainer } from "./witness-core";
export type { Witness } from "./witness-core";

import { witnessRuntime } from "./witness-runtime";

let instance: Witness | null | undefined;
/** Null on ordinary launches and outside an iOS simulator driven by `snapback4 witness ios`. */
export function witness(): Witness | null {
  if (instance === undefined) {
    const container = requireOptionalNativeModule<WitnessContainer>("Snapback4");
    instance = container?.witnessLaunch && JSON.parse(container.witnessLaunch).smoke === true ? null : createWitness(container, witnessRuntime());
  }
  return instance;
}

/** The starter may use normal guest sign-in during prime; never on ordinary launches. */
export function smokeSegment(): "prime" | "offline" | "restart" | null {
  const container = requireOptionalNativeModule<WitnessContainer>("Snapback4");
  if (!container?.witnessLaunch) return null;
  const config = JSON.parse(container.witnessLaunch);
  return config.smoke === true && ["prime", "offline", "restart"].includes(config.segment) ? config.segment : null;
}

/** Simulator smoke uses its owned loopback backend; ordinary launches keep the app URL. */
export function smokeOrigin(fallback: string): string {
  const container = requireOptionalNativeModule<WitnessContainer>("Snapback4");
  if (!container?.witnessLaunch) return fallback;
  const config = JSON.parse(container.witnessLaunch);
  return config.smoke === true && /^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:[0-9]+$/.test(config.origin) ? config.origin : fallback;
}

/** Disposable account supplied only by the owned prime smoke launch. */
export function smokeAccount(): { email: string; password: string } | null {
  const container = requireOptionalNativeModule<WitnessContainer>("Snapback4");
  if (!container?.witnessLaunch) return null;
  const config = JSON.parse(container.witnessLaunch);
  return config.smoke === true && config.segment === "prime" && typeof config.smokeAccount?.email === "string" && typeof config.smokeAccount?.password === "string" ? config.smokeAccount : null;
}

//! Starter leftovers on the init-first path: `init --web` (or `--expo`) wrote
//! the todo starter, then the project replaced `snapback/schema.q`. The
//! starter's own files that still match the bytes init wrote, but no longer
//! fit the schema, are leftovers: `check` names them and `init --adapt`
//! removes or rewrites them. A file the project changed is never touched.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.2 — leftovers are judged by the starter's original bytes, never by name alone.
use super::starter::{self, Body, Platform};
use super::{OwnSchema, own_schema};
use std::path::Path;

/// One unmodified starter file that no longer fits the project's schema.
pub(crate) struct Leftover {
    pub path: &'static str,
    pub why: String,
    /// The text `init --adapt` writes; `None` removes the file.
    pub rewrite: Option<String>,
}

/// Starter operations its fixtures, cases and `Todos` screen call.
const STARTER_OPERATIONS: [&str; 4] = ["list", "add", "toggle", "remove"];

/// Whether a schema still has the starter's `todos` table and the operations
/// its fixtures, cases and `Todos` screen call.
pub(super) fn fits_todos(own: &OwnSchema) -> bool {
    own.tables.iter().any(|table| table == "todos")
        && STARTER_OPERATIONS.iter().all(|op| own.operations.iter().any(|name| name == op))
}

/// What the schema in `dir` leaves of the starter, and the advice that goes
/// with it (a sign-in the project must write by hand). No schema: nothing.
pub(crate) fn leftovers(dir: &Path) -> (Vec<Leftover>, Vec<String>) {
    let (found, advice, _) = plan(dir);
    (found, advice)
}

fn plan(dir: &Path) -> (Vec<Leftover>, Vec<String>, Vec<String>) {
    let Ok(Some(own)) = own_schema(dir) else { return (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new()) };
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    let mut advice = Vec::new();
    let mut modified = Vec::new();
    let todos = fits_todos(&own);
    for (path, text) in starter::FIXTURES {
        let current = read(dir, path);
        if current.as_ref().is_some_and(|current| *current != super::without_design_references(text)) { modified.push(path.to_owned()); }
        if !todos && current.is_some_and(|current| current == super::without_design_references(text)) {
            let what = if path.ends_with("todos.jsonl") { "rows for the todo starter's `todos` table" } else { "cases for the todo starter's list/add/toggle/remove" };
            found.push(Leftover { path, why: format!("the unmodified {what}; your snapback/*.q has no todos table with those operations, so `snapback4 test` would refuse it"), rewrite: None });
        }
    }
    for platform in [Platform::Web, Platform::Expo] {
        if !screens(dir, platform, &own, todos, &mut found, &mut advice) {
            for path in [platform.paths().0, platform.paths().1] { if read(dir, path).is_some() { modified.push(path.to_owned()); } }
        }
    }
    if let Some(text) = read(dir, "src/native-smoke.ts") {
        let wanted = starter::native_smoke(own.identity.is_some_and(|(password, guests)| password && !guests));
        let recognized = if std::fs::symlink_metadata(dir.join("src/native-smoke.ts")).is_ok_and(|m| m.file_type().is_symlink()) { None } else { super::proof_advice::native_template(&text) };
        if recognized.is_none() { modified.push("src/native-smoke.ts".to_owned()); }
        if recognized.is_some() && !smoke_referenced(dir, &found) {
            found.push(Leftover { path: "src/native-smoke.ts", why: "the unmodified helper is now supplied by snapback4-expo/native-smoke; the planned screens no longer import this copy".into(), rewrite: None });
        } else if text != wanted && let Some((version, password)) = recognized && smoke_referenced(dir, &found) {
            let old = text != starter::native_smoke(password);
            let why = if old {
                let mode = if password != own.identity.is_some_and(|(password, guests)| password && !guests) { "; refresh also updates its sign-in mode" } else { "" };
                format!("an older starter version ({version}; adapt can refresh it){mode}")
            } else {
                "the unmodified native smoke helper uses a different starter sign-in mode (adapt can refresh it)".into()
            };
            found.push(Leftover { path: "src/native-smoke.ts", why, rewrite: Some(wanted) });
        }
    }
    if read(dir, "src/native-smoke.ts").is_some() && !smoke_referenced(dir, &found) && !found.iter().any(|f| f.path == "src/native-smoke.ts" && f.rewrite.is_none()) {
        advice.push("info: src/native-smoke.ts has no source reference; review it before a native smoke proof".into());
    }
    if !todos && let Some(web) = [false, true].into_iter().find(|web| super::proof_advice::frontend_template(dir, *web).is_some_and(|(_, template)| template.is_none())) {
        found.push(Leftover { path: "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs", why: "the unmodified todo proof needs your screen's write assertions; keep a runnable frontend scaffold that explicitly reports the missing scenario".into(), rewrite: Some(super::proof::frontend_scaffold(web)) });
    }
    readme(dir, &own, todos, &mut found, &mut modified);
    app_json(dir, &mut found);
    expo_favicon(dir, &mut found);
    (found, advice, modified)
}

// A custom entry/component/proof can reference the helper too. Generated trees
// and dependency directories are not authored source; do not follow symlinks.
fn smoke_referenced(root: &Path, changes: &[Leftover]) -> bool {
    fn walk(root: &Path, dir: &Path, helper: &Path, changes: &[Leftover]) -> bool {
        let Ok(entries)=std::fs::read_dir(dir) else { return true; };
        for entry in entries {
            let Ok(entry)=entry else {return true;};
            let Ok(kind)=entry.file_type() else {return true;};
            let path=entry.path();
            if kind.is_symlink() {
                if matches!(entry.file_name().to_str(),Some("node_modules"|".git"|".snapback4"|".expo"|"target"|"dist"|"build"|"generated")) {continue;}
                return true; // Unknown source may refer back to the local helper.
            }
            if kind.is_dir() {
                if !matches!(entry.file_name().to_str(),Some("node_modules"|".git"|".snapback4"|".expo"|"target"|"dist"|"build"|"generated")) && walk(root,&path,helper,changes) {return true;}
            } else if path!=helper && !path.to_string_lossy().ends_with(".d.ts")
                && path.extension().and_then(|e|e.to_str()).is_some_and(|e|matches!(e,"ts"|"tsx"|"js"|"jsx"|"mjs"|"cjs")) {
                let relative = path.strip_prefix(root).unwrap().to_string_lossy();
                let text = if let Some(change) = changes.iter().find(|f| f.path == relative) {
                    let Some(text) = &change.rewrite else { continue; }; Some(text.clone())
                } else { std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok() };
                if text.is_none_or(|text|text.replace("snapback4-expo/native-smoke", "").contains("native-smoke")) {return true;}
            }
        }
        false
    }
    walk(root,root,&root.join("src/native-smoke.ts"),changes)
}

/// The starter README, while it is still one init wrote (for either screen,
/// at the ports it names), when it describes another screen than the schema
/// now gets: the Todos README beside a project's schema, or the reverse.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.4 — wave 6 (042): adapt rewrote the screen but left a README about todos and guest sign-in.
fn readme(dir: &Path, own: &OwnSchema, todos: bool, found: &mut Vec<Leftover>, modified: &mut Vec<String>) {
    let platform = if dir.join("src/App.tsx").is_file() { Platform::Web } else if dir.join("App.tsx").is_file() { Platform::Expo } else { return };
    let title = super::title(dir);
    let personas = own.identity.is_none() && !own.personas.is_empty();
    let wanted_body = if todos { Body::Todos } else { Body::Home(None) };
    for path in ["README.md", "README.snapback.md"] {
        let Some(text) = read(dir, path) else { continue };
        let port = number_after(&text, "127.0.0.1:");
        let web_port = number_after(&text, "localhost:");
        let ports = [(port, web_port), (None, web_port), (port, None), (None, None)];
        // The offline paragraph names the schema's synced tables when init
        // wrote it; any of them (or 0.4.22's unconditional claim) still matches.
        let masked = starter::without_offline(&text);
        let explicit_online = platform == Platform::Web && read(dir, "src/client.ts").is_some_and(|client| client.contains("writes: \"online\""));
        let matched = ports.into_iter().find(|&(port, web_port)| {
            [(Body::Todos, false), (Body::Home(None), false), (Body::Home(None), true)].iter()
                .any(|(body, personas)| [false, true].iter().any(|password| [false, true].iter().any(|online| {
                    let readme = starter::identity_readme(platform, &title, body, *personas, &starter::Offline::Unknown, *password);
                    let readme = if *online { starter::online_readme(&readme) } else { readme };
                    masked == starter::without_offline(&super::localize(path, &super::without_design_references(&readme), port, web_port))
                })))
        });
        let Some((port, web_port)) = matched else { modified.push(path.to_owned()); continue };
        let wanted = super::localize(path, &super::without_design_references(&starter::identity_readme(platform, &title, &wanted_body, personas, &own.offline, own.identity.is_some_and(|(password, guests)| password && !guests))), port, web_port);
        let wanted = if explicit_online { starter::online_readme(&wanted) } else { wanted };
        let wanted = if todos { super::proof::readme(wanted) } else { wanted };
        if wanted == text { continue; }
        let about = if todos { "the todo starter's operations, which your snapback/*.q declares again" } else { "your snapback/*.q and the Home screen, named after this directory" };
        let only_proof = super::proof::without_readme(&wanted) == text;
        let only_offline = !text.starts_with("# Todos") && starter::without_offline(&wanted) == masked;
        // A schema that does not compile right now says nothing about what it syncs.
        if only_offline && !only_proof && own.offline == starter::Offline::Unknown { continue; }
        let why = if only_proof {
            "the unmodified starter README lacks frontend/day-two proof instructions; adapt adds them".to_owned()
        } else if only_offline {
            "the unmodified starter README says what works offline for another schema; adapt rewrites that paragraph from the tables your snapback/*.q syncs".to_owned()
        } else {
            format!("the unmodified starter README describes {}; adapt rewrites it to describe {about}", if text.starts_with("# Todos") { "the todo starter (its todos table and guest sign-in)" } else { "the Home screen for another schema" })
        };
        found.push(Leftover { path, why, rewrite: Some(wanted) });
    }
}

/// An Expo `app.json` that still carries the todo starter's slug, scheme and
/// bundle ids (written by 0.4.21 and earlier): adapt names them after the
/// directory and changes nothing else in the file.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.4 — wave 6 (067): adapted Expo apps kept dev.snapback4.todos.
fn app_json(dir: &Path, found: &mut Vec<Leftover>) {
    let Some(text) = read(dir, "app.json") else { return };
    let Ok(config) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&text) else { return };
    let expo = &config["expo"];
    let [(_, slug), (_, scheme), (_, bundle)] = starter::TODO_IDS;
    if expo["slug"] != slug || expo["scheme"] != scheme || expo["ios"]["bundleIdentifier"] != bundle || expo["android"]["package"] != bundle { return; }
    let (new_slug, new_scheme, new_bundle) = starter::app_ids(&super::title(dir));
    let quoted = |value: &str| format!("\"{value}\"");
    let rewrite = text.replace(&quoted(bundle), &quoted(&new_bundle)).replace(&quoted(slug), &quoted(&new_slug)).replace(&quoted(scheme), &quoted(&new_scheme));
    found.push(Leftover { path: "app.json", why: format!("the todo starter's ids (slug {slug}, scheme {scheme}, bundle id {bundle}); adapt names them after this directory ({new_slug}, {new_scheme}, {new_bundle})"), rewrite: Some(rewrite) });
}

### 15.2 Lookup contract and diagnostics

Wave-20 advice amendment: LLP 3000.000.000.001 §10 extends N_LOOKUP_FILTERED
to asserted/same-table reads, preferring an existing N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN at the
same site; private unique source advice preserves the public refusal boundary.

Keep one point-read spelling. **`t[key]` returns the readable row or null**
for absent, hidden or expired rows. **`t[key] ! else CODE` refuses with CODE**
for the same three cases. This applies in queries and mutations and through
helpers. `exists t[key]` in a program is caller-visible; a rule's `exists`
is the separate rule-witness mechanism (§14.1). An id never grants authority.
There is no new optional-lookup operator or hidden-row error: the optional
form already exists. A later require cannot replace an earlier refusal.

Public refusal data must never distinguish hidden from missing, name a
runtime hiding clause only on a hit, disclose a key, or change a refusal's
meter according to existence. Static check diagnostics may quote authored
rules and source locations: they depend only on source, not stored rows.
Developer refusal traces remain local operator evidence. A blind write is
not a lookup and must not acquire a warning suggesting wider read access.

Extend program lookup advice beyond required same-table write targets.
**N_LOOKUP_FILTERED** identifies a mutation's optional point read of a
non-public side table (a table the operation does not write) when its key and
current binder flow facts do not prove read authority. Required direct point
reads keep existing N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN advice rather than duplicate this note;
the assertion already makes refusal explicit. It names
the operation, source point, target read rule and its declaration, and the
consequence (null before a later field/default or require).
Use the binder's actual point/key and current flow proofs, including helpers;
read-through side tables are included and name their authored inherited rule.
Ephemeral and maintained-value reads retain their specialized existing advice.
Captured helper arguments transport diagnostic-only exact-point facts (including
through nested helpers), plus known viewer identities. These markers cannot
establish runtime authority, non-null typing or prediction eligibility; key
rebinding and writes invalidate exact-point advice facts. The transfer walk is
bounded (512 visited expression nodes, depth 32); exhaustion declines the
suppression proof, never a runtime read or authority check;
never infer the read from a blind write target. Exact key pins that decide
read authority, a dominating readable lookup/guard, direct asserted reads and
lookups of the operation's written tables stay quiet. Rule constants are normalized before key substitution, and the target-row
namespace is sealed before injecting caller expressions: an unpinned target
field cannot borrow an enclosing shape's focal row or a caller binding.
This is missing-proof advice, not a claim all callers are denied. Repeated instances
are located, and advice suggests a deliberately reader-visible projection or
an earlier authorized gate; it never mechanically widens a private rule.
Existing N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN remains the more specific required write-target note;
avoid duplicate notes for that source site.

The rules card carries this lookup/refusal ladder and explicitly separates
program probes from rule probes. An executable packed-package qualification
runs every newly added/changed Quarry example as written and checks absent,
hidden, readable and expired rows plus statement precedence. Existing
SEC/SEC3 existence-oracle lints keep their source-level scope: a readable
row's custom later failure can intentionally reveal its existence, while
hidden and absent remain equivalent. SEC4 owns security-analysis changes.

## 4. Staging clock

Wave-20 reporting amendment: LLP 3000.000.000.001 §10 changes the proof
advance return to `{now, fired, held}` and explains persisted boundary holds;
operator authority and clock execution semantics below are unchanged.

Only a store durably classified staging by deploy --staging may serve with
--clock-offset. Missing/unknown classification is production. This setting
is process-local, with the same signed-duration parser and monotone elapsed
clock as dev. No serve-time mechanism can reclassify an existing production store. Restart drops the offset unless explicitly
provided again; persisted timed-disclosure floors never retreat below their captured value.

Staging exposes the existing /dev/clock/status and /dev/clock/advance only
with any full service session: these are trusted operator credentials, as for
system jobs. Production refuses even with a service token, and an explicit
production serve offset refuses with E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY before listener startup. Account, guest, read-only and unauthenticated
requests refuse. Recheck classification and session under the engine writer
before advancing. All fixture, reset, persona and dev-job doors remain closed.
Use the same advance implementation, schedule drain and ambiguous-reply law
as dev. CLI clock advance --release DIR mints its local service authority.
startServe accepts clockOffset and exposes now()/advance() through that
operator authority; it never changes store classification. Each helper control
mints a current staging-time operator session rather than caching a credential
across arbitrary time jumps. Ordinary user sessions retain normal expiry.

the persisted disclosure floor, and passes that one time through the core's
explicit `adopt_release_at`. A live preview probes the existing filesystem owner lock independently of
HTTP bind/address hints and acquires a stopped-store lock before taking its
SQLite snapshot, retaining that lock through inspection. A rollback preview
reuses its caller's existing ownership rather than probing its own lock as a
live host.
A live preview samples time through the same-owner,
store-bound existing private status protocol; no session is minted or clock
changed. A missing existing-store ownership sidecar refuses rather than assuming a
stopped host without exclusion; ordinary rollback preview can reestablish and
reuse its canonical ownership. A revision mismatch with the private database snapshot refuses as a
racing activation. Store contents and the clock are point-in-time samples, not
a freeze of later live writes. A stopped store's cold activation/preview uses
wall time, with the existing persisted disclosure floor applied by activation.

 * Guards take `page.read`; `matchRead` also accepts the whole page. */
export interface PageHook<R extends readonly unknown[]> {
  items: R[number][];
  hasMore: boolean;
  read: Read<R>;
  loadMore: () => void;
}
/** What `usePage(op, args)` returns, named by the operation, for props:
 * `function More({ page }: { page: UsePage<typeof api.thread> })`. */
export type UsePage<O> = O extends Query<any, any> ? ResultOf<O> extends readonly unknown[] ? PageHook<ResultOf<O>> : never : never;

/** A query `usePage` can page: it takes its cursor as `c` (`c: cursor ?` in
 * the schema) and reads `after c`. Any other query names the fix in its error. */
type PagedQuery<A, R> = Query<A, R> & ("c" extends keyof A ? unknown
  : { readonly "usePage needs a query that declares `c: cursor ?` and reads `after c`; see `snapback4 guide reads`": true });

/** Own the current requested cursor chain. A changed/withdrawn cursor releases
 * its old suffix. Mount this hook in an active route child; keep the composer
 * outside that child and bound point-reader IDs to requested pages/visible rows.
 * See the bounded screen recipe in CLIENT-AND-OPERATIONS.md.
 */
export function usePage<A, R extends readonly unknown[]>(op: PagedQuery<A, R>, args: Omit<A, "c">, options?: ReadHookOptions): PageHook<R> {
  const client = useClient();
  const skip = options?.skip === true;
  const key = skip ? null : readKey(op, args);
  const paged = op as Query<A & { c?: Cursor | null }, R>;
  const pages = useMemo(() => skip ? SKIPPED_PAGES : new Pages(client, paged, args as A & { c?: Cursor | null }, observeOptions(options)), [client, op, key, options?.keep, skip]); // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  const snapshot = useSyncExternalStore(pages.subscribe, pages.getSnapshot, pages.getSnapshot);
  return { items: snapshot.items as R[number][], hasMore: snapshot.hasMore, read: snapshot.read as Read<R>, loadMore: pages.loadMore };
}
/** The page chain a skipped `usePage` holds: loading, no items, nothing to load. */
const SKIPPED_PAGE_SNAPSHOT = { items: [] as never[], hasMore: false, read: LOADING };
const SKIPPED_PAGES = { subscribe: () => () => {}, getSnapshot: () => SKIPPED_PAGE_SNAPSHOT, loadMore: () => {} };

/** Complete online Following history; the SDK owns preparation and replay. */
export function useFollowing<A, R extends readonly unknown[]>(op: FollowingQuery<A, R>, args: A) {
  const client = useClient(), key = readKey(op, args);
  const following = useMemo(() => new Following(client, op, args), [client, op, key]); // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  const snapshot = useSyncExternalStore(following.subscribe, following.getSnapshot, following.getSnapshot);
  return { ...snapshot, loadMore: following.loadMore, retry: following.retry, refresh: following.refresh };
}

/** A write. `run` never throws; `last` is the most recent outcome, including
 * queued settlement. A sent replay has `replayed: true` and no result. */
export interface MutationHook<A, Outcome> {
  run(args: A): Promise<Outcome>;
  last: Outcome | undefined;
  inFlight: boolean;
}
/** A durable write's hook: `run` waits for sent/failed independently of read
 * subscriptions and component lifetime. Offline it waits for reconnect.
 * Explicit `{ waitSeconds: 0 }` returns at custody; `{ id }` reuses saved intent. */
export interface WriteHook<A, R> {
  run(args: A, options?: MutateOptions): Promise<Write<R>>;
  /** Undefined before the first run. `isFailed(last)` narrows to the refusal
   * (`last.why`); `sentResult(last)` is the fresh result, if any (a replayed
   * receipt has none). */
  last: Write<R> | undefined;
  inFlight: boolean;
}
/** What `useMutation(op)` returns, named by the operation, for props:
 * `function Row({ remove }: { remove: UseMutation<typeof api.remove> })`. */
export type UseMutation<O> = O extends Ephemeral<infer A, infer R> ? MutationHook<A, Signal<R>>
  : O extends Mutation<infer A, infer R> ? WriteHook<A, R> : never;
function useTrackedMutation<A, R>(op: Ephemeral<A, R>): MutationHook<A, Signal<R>>;
function useTrackedMutation<A, R>(op: Mutation<A, R>, id?: string): WriteHook<A, R> & { restoring: boolean };
function useTrackedMutation<A, R>(op: Mutation<A, R> | Ephemeral<A, R>, id?: string): MutationHook<A, Write<R> | Signal<R>> | WriteHook<A, R>;
function useTrackedMutation<A, R>(op: Mutation<A, R> | Ephemeral<A, R>, id?: string): MutationHook<A, Write<R> | Signal<R>> & { restoring?: boolean } {
  const client = useClient();
  const [last, setLast] = useState<Write<R> | Signal<R> | undefined>(undefined);
  const [inFlight, setInFlight] = useState(false);

// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#10 — packed starters must pass their real web toolchains
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { createServer } from "node:net";
import { Worker } from "node:worker_threads";
import { loadavg } from "node:os";
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { setTimeout as sleep } from "node:timers/promises";
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, existsSync, rmSync } from "node:fs";

// The live keeper alone signals its own group. Closing its private pipe also
// cleans up if this runner dies; no cached PID ever authorizes a signal.
export async function runToolchainCommand(command, args, { cwd, env, timeout }) {
  const owner = fileURLToPath(new URL("./test-command-owner.mjs", import.meta.url));
  const keeper = spawn(process.execPath, [owner, "100", command, ...args], { cwd, env, detached: true, stdio: ["pipe", "inherit", "inherit", "ipc"] });
  let released = false, completed = false, failure, status;
  const release = mode => { if (!released) { released = true; keeper.stdin.end(mode); } };
  const fail = error => { failure ??= error; release("TERM"); };
  const timer = setTimeout(() => fail(Error(`${command}: toolchain command timed out`)), timeout);
  keeper.stdin.on("error", error => { failure ??= error; });
  keeper.on("message", message => {
    if (message.error) fail(Error(message.error));
    if (message.exited) { completed = true; status = message.status; release("KILL"); }
  });
  await new Promise(done => {
    keeper.once("error", error => { failure ??= error; });
    keeper.once("close", done);
  });
  clearTimeout(timer);
  if (!released || !completed) failure ??= Error(`${command}: command owner exited without a result`);
  // This read-only group-existence probe needs no /proc mount in the clean
  // userspace. Refuse on lingering members or ambiguous/permission errors.
  // Two empty observations also protect against a transient inspection result.
  const deadline = performance.now() + 5_000;
  let empty = 0;
  if (keeper.pid) while (empty < 2) {
    try { process.kill(-keeper.pid, 0); empty = 0; }
    catch (error) { if (error.code === "ESRCH") empty++; else { failure ??= error; break; } }
    if (empty === 2) break;
    if (performance.now() >= deadline) { failure ??= Error(`${command}: toolchain process group did not drain`); break; }
    await sleep(50);
  }
  if (failure) throw failure;
  if (status !== 0) throw Error(`${command}: toolchain command exited ${status}`);
}

async function boundedStop(work, label) {
  let timer;
  try { return await Promise.race([work, new Promise((_, reject) => { timer = setTimeout(() => reject(Error(label + " timed out")), 10_000); })]); }
  finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
}
export async function proveFrontendTwice(run, cwd, starter) {
  const results = [];
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 2; attempt++) {
    const occupied = createServer();
    const low = await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { occupied.once("error", reject); occupied.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => resolve(occupied.address().port)); });
    const high = Math.min(65535, low + 20);
    const workers = Array.from({ length: 2 }, () => new Worker(`setInterval(() => { const until = performance.now() + 25; while (performance.now() < until) {} }, 50);`, { eval: true }));
    const started = Date.now(), load = loadavg();
    const audit = join(cwd, `listener-audit-${attempt}.json`);
    const trace = join(cwd, `listener-audit-${attempt}.trace`);
    const auditEnabled = process.platform === "linux";
    const tracerVersion = auditEnabled ? (await import("./proof-listener-audit.mjs")).requireListenerTracer() : undefined;
    const proofLogs = join(cwd, `proof-logs-${attempt}`);
    try {
      rmSync(join(cwd, "dist"), { recursive: true, force: true });
      await run(auditEnabled ? "strace" : process.execPath, [...(auditEnabled ? ["-f", "-q", "-z", "-yy", "-e", "trace=listen", "-e", "signal=none", "-o", trace, process.execPath] : []), "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs"], cwd, { PORT_LO: String(low), PORT_HI: String(high), SNAPBACK4_PROOF_LOGS: proofLogs });
      const listenerAudit = auditEnabled ? (await import("./proof-listener-audit.mjs")).auditListenerTrace(readFileSync(trace, "utf8"), low, high) : { status: "not-run", reason: "listener audit belongs to Linux qualification" };
      if (auditEnabled) { assert.equal(listenerAudit.status, "passed"); assert.ok(listenerAudit.samples > 0); listenerAudit.tracerVersion = tracerVersion; }
      assert.ok(existsSync(proofLogs));
      writeFileSync(audit, JSON.stringify(listenerAudit));
      results.push({ starter: starter.id, kind: starter.kind, attempt, status: "passed", elapsedMs: Date.now() - started, range: [low, high], occupied: low, cpuLoadWorkers: workers.length, loadavg: load, listenerAudit, logs: proofLogs });
    } finally {
      const stopped = await Promise.allSettled([...workers.map(worker => boundedStop(worker.terminate(), "CPU worker stop")), boundedStop(new Promise(resolve => occupied.close(resolve)), "occupied listener close")]);
      const failures = stopped.filter(result => result.status === "rejected").map(result => result.reason);
      if (failures.length) throw new AggregateError(failures, "loaded-host proof cleanup failed");
    }
  }
  return results;
}

    : `<View nativeID="proof-rows"><ProofTextInput accessibilityLabel="Task" value={draft} onChangeText={setDraft}/><Button title="Add" onPress={()=>void writer.run({title:draft})}/><Text>{"data" in rows?JSON.stringify(rows.data):""}</Text></View>`;

import { pendingRead, readyRead } from "./read-existence.ts";
import type { Client, Query, Read, Observed, ObserveOptions, Cursor } from "./contract.ts";
import { isReady } from "./contract.ts";
import { peekObservation } from "./observe-watch.ts";
const LOADING: Read<never> = { loading: true };

/** The requested page chain, with one newest observed image per row ID. */
export class Pages<A extends { c?: Cursor | null }, R extends readonly unknown[]> {
  private pages: { cursor: Cursor | null; observed: Observed<R>; unsubscribe: () => void }[] = [];
  private requested = 1;
  private subs = new Set<() => void>();
  private cache: { items: R[number][]; hasMore: boolean; read: Read<R> } | null = null;
  private peeked: Read<R> | undefined;
  private cacheReads: Read<R>[] = [];
  private reconciling = false;
  private imageRevision = 0;
  private imageRevisions = new WeakMap<object, number>();
  private noteImage(read: Read<R>) {
    // Revalidation/freshness changes retain the same data array; they do not
    // make an older row image newer than an image delivered on another page.
    if (isReady(read) && Array.isArray(read.data) && !this.imageRevisions.has(read.data))
      this.imageRevisions.set(read.data, ++this.imageRevision);
    return read;
  }
  constructor(private client: Client, private op: Query<A, R>, private args: A, private options?: ObserveOptions) {}
  private open(c: Cursor | null) {
    const observed = this.client.observe(this.op, { ...this.args, c }, this.options);
    const page = { cursor: c, observed, unsubscribe: () => {} };
    this.pages.push(page);
    page.unsubscribe = observed.subscribe(() => {
      if (this.pages.includes(page)) this.notify();
    });
  }
  private drop(from: number) {
    for (const page of this.pages.splice(from)) {
      page.unsubscribe();
      page.observed.close();
    }
  }
  private notify() {
    if (this.reconciling) return;
    this.reconciling = true;
    try {
      // A later page belongs to its predecessor's current cursor. Keep the
      // requested depth, but discard the old suffix before opening a new one:
      // deduplication alone cannot recover rows an old boundary skipped.
      for (let i = 0; i < this.pages.length; i++) {
        const read = this.noteImage(this.pages[i]!.observed.getSnapshot());
        const next = isReady(read) && Array.isArray(read.data) ? read.next : null;
        if (!next || i + 1 >= this.requested || this.pages.slice(0, i + 1).some((p) => p.cursor === next)) {
          this.drop(i + 1);
          break;
        }
        if (this.pages[i + 1]?.cursor !== next) {
          this.drop(i + 1);
          this.open(next);
        }
      }
      this.cache = null;
    } finally { this.reconciling = false; }
    for (const s of this.subs) s();
  }
  subscribe = (notify: () => void) => {
    this.subs.add(notify);
    if (!this.pages.length) { this.open(null); this.notify(); }
    let active = true;
    return () => {
      if (!active) return;
      active = false;
      this.subs.delete(notify);
      if (!this.subs.size) { this.drop(0); this.cache = null; }
    };
  };
  getSnapshot = () => {
    const peeked = this.pages.length ? undefined : peekObservation(this.client, this.op, { ...this.args, c: null }, this.options);
    // An unsubscribed render owns no notifications: recheck the live snapshot
    // and the linger cutoff on every call, caching only its derived page shape.
    if (peeked !== this.peeked) { this.peeked = peeked; this.cache = null; }
    // @ref LLP 3000.023#5 — page accessors check deadlines before a combined cache can escape.
    let sources, reads: Read<R>[];
    do {
      sources = [...this.pages];
      reads = sources.length ? sources.map(page => this.noteImage(page.observed.getSnapshot())) : peeked ? [this.noteImage(peeked)] : [];
      // A deadline check may synchronously drop a suffix through notify().
    } while (sources.length !== this.pages.length || sources.some((page, i) => page !== this.pages[i]));
    if (reads.length !== this.cacheReads.length || reads.some((read, i) => read !== this.cacheReads[i])) this.cache = null;
    this.cacheReads = reads;
    if (this.cache) return this.cache;
    const items: R[number][] = [];
    const identities = new Map<string, { index: number; revision: number }>();
    let last: Read<R> = LOADING as Read<R>;
    let complete = true, fresh = true, revalidating = false, pending = false;
    let cut: import("./contract.ts").ReadCut = null;
    let since: number | undefined;
    let knownSince = true;
    let loadingMore = false;
    for (const read of reads) {
      // @ref LLP 3000.019#3.3 — a pending next page keeps the ready prefix on screen.
      // Resets of the first page and refusals still replace the combined read.
      if ("loading" in read && isReady(last)) { loadingMore = true; break; }
      last = read;
      if (!isReady(read)) break;
      if (!Array.isArray(read.data)) { last = LOADING as Read<R>; break; }
      // @ref LLP 3000.028#3.3 — keyset edits may repeat IDs across pages.
      // Keep the first display position and the most recently observed image,
      // including a refreshed earlier page. Only compiler-proved source row IDs are accumulation keys; arbitrary
      // projections preserve ordinary list semantics, including a field named id.
      const revision = this.imageRevisions.get(read.data)!;
      for (const item of read.data as readonly R[number][]) {
        const id = this.op.rowKey === "id" && item && typeof item === "object" && "id" in item ? item.id : undefined;
        const previous = typeof id === "string" ? identities.get(id) : undefined;
        if (previous) {
          if (revision >= previous.revision) {
            items[previous.index] = item;
            previous.revision = revision;
          }
        } else {
          if (typeof id === "string") identities.set(id, { index: items.length, revision });
          items.push(item);
        }
      }
      pending ||= pendingRead(read);
      complete &&= read.complete;
      if (read.cut === "meter" || (cut === null && read.cut === "words")) cut = read.cut;
      fresh &&= read.fresh;
      revalidating ||= read.revalidating === true;
      if (!read.fresh) {
        if (read.since == null) knownSince = false;
        else since = Math.min(since ?? read.since, read.since);
      }
    }
    const hasMore = !loadingMore && isReady(last) && last.next != null && !this.pages.some((p) => p.cursor === last.next);
    const read: Read<R> = isReady(last)
      ? readyRead({ data: items as unknown as R, complete, cut, fresh, ...(revalidating ? { revalidating: true } : {}), ...(knownSince && since != null ? { since } : {}), next: last.next ?? null }, pending || loadingMore)
      : last;
    this.cache = { items, hasMore, read };
    return this.cache;
  };
  loadMore = () => {
    if (!this.subs.size || !this.getSnapshot().hasMore) return;
    this.requested = Math.max(this.requested, this.pages.length + 1);
    this.notify();
  };
}

/// UTC calendar text for Unix milliseconds: schedule boundaries are UTC.
pub fn utc(ms: i64) -> String {
    let (days, rem) = (ms.div_euclid(86_400_000), ms.rem_euclid(86_400_000));
    // Civil-from-days (proleptic Gregorian), exact for the I53 range.
    let z = days + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let doe = z - era * 146_097;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1_460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let day = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let month = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let year = yoe + era * 400 + i64::from(month <= 2);
    format!("{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}Z", rem / 3_600_000, rem % 3_600_000 / 60_000, rem % 60_000 / 1_000)
}

/// A positive duration in the units `clock advance` accepts, rounded up to a second.
pub fn span(ms: i64) -> String {
    let seconds = (ms.max(0) + 999) / 1_000;
    let (d, h, m, s) = (seconds / 86_400, seconds % 86_400 / 3_600, seconds % 3_600 / 60, seconds % 60);
    let parts: Vec<String> = [(d, "d"), (h, "h"), (m, "m"), (s, "s")].into_iter().filter(|(n, _)| *n > 0).map(|(n, unit)| format!("{n}{unit}")).collect();
    if parts.is_empty() { "0s".into() } else { parts.join("") }
}

/// Each schedule's saved boundary, in declaration order.
pub fn saved_boundaries(engine: &Engine) -> Vec<Option<i64>> {
    engine.schema().schedules.iter()
        .map(|schedule| {
            let shape = engine.store().schedule_shape(&schedule.name).ok().flatten();
            if shape.as_ref().is_some_and(|shape| *shape != snapback4_core::value::digest(schedule)) { return None; }
            engine.store().schedule_boundary(&schedule.name).ok().flatten()
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Preflight is bounded before the clock or worker leases change.
// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12.1 — only explicit execution enumerates all crossed windows; coalesced reports keep a bounded preview.
pub fn crossed_boundaries(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], now: i64, held: bool, each_boundary: bool) -> Result<Vec<(usize, i64)>, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    let mut boundaries = Vec::new();
    let mut report_bytes = 0usize;
    for (index, schedule) in engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate() {
        // JSON may escape every error byte; count that bound per schedule.
        report_bytes = report_bytes.saturating_add(2048 + 6 * (REPORT_ERROR_BYTES + 3) + 8 * (schedule.name.len() + schedule.target.len()));
        if report_bytes > REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET { return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("schedule report exceeds its byte budget; reduce the declared schedules")); }
        if held { continue; }
        let Some(old) = before.get(index).copied().flatten() else { continue; };
        let end = schedule.boundary(now);
        if old >= end { continue; }
        let periods = schedule.periods_between(old, end);
        if each_boundary && periods > (10_000 - boundaries.len()) as i64 {
            return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("--each-boundary crosses more than 10000 schedule windows; use a smaller duration or omit --each-boundary to coalesce"));
        }
        report_bytes = report_bytes.saturating_add((if each_boundary { periods as usize } else { (periods as usize).min(SKIPPED_PREVIEW + 1) }).saturating_mul(1024 + 8 * schedule.target.len()));
        if report_bytes > REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET { return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("schedule window report exceeds its byte budget; use a smaller duration")); }

// Detached readers do not take engine tickets. Sample OS load as well as the
// round-3 engine contention signal; cache the syscall for 100 ms. Load includes
// other tenants and trails short bursts, so this is a pacing hint, not admission.
fn host_contended() -> bool {
    use std::sync::{Mutex, OnceLock};
    static SAMPLE: Mutex<(Option<Instant>, bool)> = Mutex::new((None, false));
    static CPUS: OnceLock<usize> = OnceLock::new();
    let mut sample = lock(&SAMPLE);
    if sample.0.is_none_or(|at| at.elapsed() >= Duration::from_millis(100)) {
        let mut load = 0.0;
        let cpus = *CPUS.get_or_init(|| std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(1, |n| n.get()));
        sample.1 = unsafe { libc::getloadavg(&mut load, 1) } == 1 && load >= cpus as f64;
        sample.0 = Some(Instant::now());
    }
    sample.1
}

fn engine_work<T>(shared: &Shared, run: impl FnOnce(&mut snapback4_core::Engine, Duration) -> T) -> T {
    let mut engine = shared.engine.background();
    lock(&shared.readers).retry_missing(&engine);
    let budget = if engine.contended() || host_contended() { CONTENDED_TIME } else { WORK_TIME };
    let result = run(&mut engine, budget);
    // Publish from this guard: a second ordinary admission would both delay
    // notification and mistake maintenance for a newly arrived request.
    shared.publish_engine(&engine);
    result
}

fn phase<T: Default>(shared: &Shared, result: Result<T, RuntimeError>, drain: bool, name: &str) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
    match result {
        Err(error) if !drain => { super::adoption::background_failure(shared, name, &error); Ok(T::default()) }
        other => other,
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — lifetimes are swept into the partition log; missed schedule boundaries fire once.
fn work(shared: &Shared, drain: bool, tick: u64) -> Result<Work, RuntimeError> {
    work_at(shared, drain, tick, None)
}

fn work_at(shared: &Shared, drain: bool, tick: u64, schedule_sample: Option<i64>) -> Result<Work, RuntimeError> {
    let mut work = Work::default();
    shared.ephemeral.sweep(shared.now())?;
    work.delivery_chunks = delivery(shared, drain)?;
    loop {
        if phase(shared, engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| engine.run_view_chunk_for(shared.now(), budget)), drain, "view recount")?.is_none() {break;}
        work.chunks += 1;
        if !drain && work.chunks >= 500 {break;}
        std::thread::yield_now();
    }
    loop {
        let swept = phase(shared, engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| engine.sweep_expired_for(shared.now(), 2_000, budget)), drain, "the expiry sweep")?;
        work.expired += swept;
        if !drain || swept == 0 { break; }
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.2 — advancing a replay clock does not release its schedule hold.
    if !shared.hold_schedules {
        let fired = phase(shared, engine_work(shared, |engine, _| {
            // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12.2 — select advance windows before draining; admission deadlines still use the live advanced clock.
            if let Some(sample) = schedule_sample {
                let windows = engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate().map(|(index, schedule)| (index, schedule.boundary(sample))).collect::<Vec<_>>();
                let mut fired = Vec::new();
                for (index, boundary) in windows { fired.extend(engine.fire_schedule_boundary_at(shared.now(), index, boundary)?); }
                Ok(fired)
            } else { engine.fire_schedules(shared.now()) }
        }), drain, "schedules")?;
        work.schedules = fired.len();
        for name in &fired { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: schedule {name} fired"); }
        work.fired = fired;
    }
    while drain || work.chunks < 500 {
        if crate::lifecycle::stopping() { break; }
        let (run, logs) = engine_work(shared, |engine, budget| {
            let run = engine.run_job_chunk_for(shared.now(), budget);
            (run, engine.take_native_logs())
        });
        for line in logs { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: native {line}"); }
        let Some(run) = phase(shared, run, drain, "job")? else { break; };
        work.chunks += 1;
        match run.state {
            snapback4_core::JobState::Done => snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: job {} done: {} chunk{}, {} row{} written", run.name, run.chunks, if run.chunks == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, run.rows_written, if run.rows_written == 1 { "" } else { "s" }),

    }

+/// The sources a scan of literals covers: the Rust crates and the client.
+pub(super) fn sources() -> Vec<PathBuf> {
+    let root = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../..");
+    let mut files = Vec::new();
+    fn walk(dir: &Path, files: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) {
+        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(dir).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{}: {e}", dir.display())) {
+            let path = entry.unwrap().path();
+            if path.is_dir() {
+                if path.file_name().is_some_and(|n| n == "node_modules" || n == "target" || n == "dist" || n == "tests" || n == "test") {
+                    continue;
+                }
+                // Differential-test records quote the Lean model's own
+                // refusals (`E_MODEL_TYPE`), which no product path emits.
+                if path.ends_with("snapback4-difftest/cases") {
+                    continue;
+                }
+                walk(&path, files);
+            } else if path.file_name().is_some_and(|n| n.to_string_lossy().ends_with("_tests.rs") || n.to_string_lossy().ends_with(".test.mjs")) {
+                // A test module inside `src/` invents refusal codes for fixtures;
+                // this check is about the codes the product itself emits.
+                continue;
+            } else if path.extension().is_some_and(|e| e == "rs" || e == "ts" || e == "tsx" || e == "md") {
+                files.push(path);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    for dir in ["crates", "packages/snapback4/src", "packages/snapback4-expo/src"] {
+        walk(&root.join(dir), &mut files);
+    }
+    files.push(root.join("packages/snapback4/README.md"));
+    assert!(files.len() > 40, "{} source files", files.len());
+    files
+}

+/// Product and feed-recipe codes at identifier boundaries, including extracted Markdown cards.
+fn code_words(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
+    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
+    let ident = |b: u8| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'_';
+    let mut out = Vec::new();
+    let mut i = 0;
+    while i + 2 < bytes.len() {
+        let prefix = [b"E_".as_slice(), b"N_".as_slice(), b"FEED_".as_slice()].into_iter().find(|p| bytes[i..].starts_with(p));
+        if let Some(prefix) = prefix.filter(|p| bytes.get(i + p.len()).is_some_and(u8::is_ascii_uppercase) && (i == 0 || !ident(bytes[i - 1]))) {
+            let start = i;
+            let mut end = i + prefix.len();
+            while end < bytes.len() && (bytes[end].is_ascii_uppercase() || bytes[end] == b'_' || bytes[end].is_ascii_digit()) {
+                end += 1;
+            }
+            if (end >= bytes.len() || !ident(bytes[end])) && bytes[end - 1] != b'_' {
+                out.push(text[start..end].to_owned());
+            }
+            i = end;
+        } else {
+            i += 1;
+        }
+    }
+    out
+}
+
+/// Every refusal code the engine, the compiler and the client emit is one
+/// `snapback4 why` explains — the orientation's promise, tested.
+#[test]
+fn every_emitted_code_is_explained() {
+    let known = codes();
+    // The placeholder in `why`'s usage line.
+    let not_codes = ["E_CODE"];
+    let mut unexplained = BTreeMap::<String, Vec<String>>::new();
+    for file in sources() {
+        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&file).unwrap();
+        for word in code_words(&text) {
+            if !known.contains(&word.as_str()) && !not_codes.contains(&word.as_str()) {
+                unexplained.entry(word).or_default().push(file.strip_prefix(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../..")).unwrap().display().to_string());
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    for (code, files) in &mut unexplained {
+        files.sort();
+        files.dedup();

    12	// The live keeper alone signals its own group. Closing its private pipe also
    13	// cleans up if this runner dies; no cached PID ever authorizes a signal.
    14	export async function runToolchainCommand(command, args, { cwd, env, timeout }) {
    15	  const owner = fileURLToPath(new URL("./test-command-owner.mjs", import.meta.url));
    16	  const keeper = spawn(process.execPath, [owner, "100", command, ...args], { cwd, env, detached: true, stdio: ["pipe", "inherit", "inherit", "ipc"] });
    17	  let released = false, completed = false, failure, status;
    18	  const release = mode => { if (!released) { released = true; keeper.stdin.end(mode); } };
    19	  const fail = error => { failure ??= error; release("TERM"); };
    20	  const timer = setTimeout(() => fail(Error(`${command}: toolchain command timed out`)), timeout);
    21	  keeper.stdin.on("error", error => { failure ??= error; });
    22	  keeper.on("message", message => {
    23	    if (message.error) fail(Error(message.error));
    24	    if (message.exited) { completed = true; status = message.status; release("KILL"); }
    25	  });
    26	  await new Promise(done => {
    27	    keeper.once("error", error => { failure ??= error; });
    28	    keeper.once("close", done);
    29	  });
    30	  clearTimeout(timer);
    31	  if (!released || !completed) failure ??= Error(`${command}: command owner exited without a result`);
    32	  // This read-only group-existence probe needs no /proc mount in the clean
    33	  // userspace. Refuse on lingering members or ambiguous/permission errors.
    34	  // Two empty observations also protect against a transient inspection result.
    35	  const deadline = performance.now() + 5_000;
    36	  let empty = 0;
    37	  if (keeper.pid) while (empty < 2) {
    38	    try { process.kill(-keeper.pid, 0); empty = 0; }
    39	    catch (error) { if (error.code === "ESRCH") empty++; else { failure ??= error; break; } }
    40	    if (empty === 2) break;
    41	    if (performance.now() >= deadline) { failure ??= Error(`${command}: toolchain process group did not drain`); break; }
    42	    await sleep(50);
    43	  }
    44	  if (failure) throw failure;
    45	  if (status !== 0) throw Error(`${command}: toolchain command exited ${status}`);
    46	}

    57	async function boundedStop(work, label) {
    58	  let timer;
    59	  try { return await Promise.race([work, new Promise((_, reject) => { timer = setTimeout(() => reject(Error(label + " timed out")), 10_000); })]); }
    60	  finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
    61	}
